title: Calculate Your Take Home Pay Australia: From Hourly Rate to Annual Salary
description: Convert your hourly rate to annual salary for a 38-hour week. Learn about tax, super, and take home pay australia with clear examples and Fair Work figures.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, your annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52. After tax and Medicare, your take home pay depends on your total income.

faqs.q: What is the formula to convert hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard 38-hour week, annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my take home pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate, as set by the Fair Work Commission. On the timesheet, you check a box to add 25% loading. Do not type a rate that already includes loading. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 becomes $33.05 with loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid by your employer at 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. It does not reduce your take home pay. The super guarantee applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, on a $60,000 salary, super adds $7,200.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

If you know your hourly rate, you can estimate your annual gross pay using a simple formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For most full-time employees in Australia, the standard week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. So if you earn $30 per hour and work 38 hours each week, your annual gross pay is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280.

It is important to note that this is a gross figure—before tax, Medicare, and any salary sacrifice arrangements. Your actual take home pay will be lower after deductions. To get a clearer picture, use the [timesheet](/), which lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. The timesheet then calculates your annual, fortnightly, and weekly amounts, and estimates tax and super.

## Understanding Your Take Home Pay Australia

Your **take home pay australia** is the amount you receive after the Australian Taxation Office deducts income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, most residents pay a Medicare levy of 2% of their taxable income. The Medicare levy reduction thresholds for singles in 2025–26 are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of preparation. This means your estimated take home pay may differ slightly from your actual pay.

For example, on a gross annual salary of $59,280, your tax would be approximately $5,292 (using the 30% bracket after the tax-free threshold) plus Medicare of $1,185.60, leaving a take home pay of about $52,802.40 per year. That works out to roughly $1,015 per week or $2,030 per fortnight.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many Australian employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, simply multiply your weekly gross by two. Using the same $30 per hour example, weekly gross is $30 × 38 = $1,140, so fortnightly gross is $2,280. After tax and Medicare, your fortnightly take home pay would be around $2,030. This can help you plan your budget and compare with salary offers that are quoted per year or per fortnight.

## The Role of Superannuation and Casual Loading

Superannuation is a compulsory contribution your employer makes on top of your salary. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is paid in addition to your gross pay—it does not reduce your take home pay. For example, on a $59,280 salary, your employer would contribute an extra $7,113.60 to your super fund.

### Casual Loading

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a casual loading of 25% on top of the base hourly rate, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. On the [timesheet](/), you can check a box to add 25% casual loading. **Do not** type a rate that already includes the loading; the tool adds it for you. For instance, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees. With casual loading, it becomes $33.05 per hour.

### Award Rates and the National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. However, most industries have award rates that are higher. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award. The figures here are based on the National Minimum Wage and the ABS Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026), which show full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week. This is an average, not a median for any specific job. For your own job, check the relevant award or enterprise agreement.

The tool then estimates your take home pay using the 2026–27 tax rates and Medicare. It also shows the super contribution your employer would pay on top.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

By understanding these components, you can better compare job offers, negotiate your salary, and plan your finances. Whether you are a permanent employee or a casual worker, knowing your **take home pay australia** helps you make informed decisions.
